title: Malformed, oversized and nonfinite clouds
symptom: Malformed rows, missing fields, excessive point counts or NaNs could make point-cloud conversion unsafe or misleading.
explanation: A PointCloud2 message has a binary layout. Validate dimensions, strides, field bounds and capacity before conversion; is_dense alone is not proof that points are finite.
steps: Check width, height, point_step, row_step and exact data length.
Require nonoverlapping scalar little-endian FLOAT32 x/y/z/intensity fields.
Reject point or byte capacity overflow before allocation.
Remove nonfinite points even when is_dense is true.
Require a finite positive intensity divisor and clear stale packed output on failure.
verification: The fresh production-code probe printed exact layout, capacity, missing-field, endian and divisor rejections. Repairing row_step accepted four points; inserting one NaN packed three. All 11 existing ROS data controls passed.
remaining_limit: Finite all-zero invalid returns are not removed here. Total point limits do not enforce the internal pillar limits.
visual_suggestion: Use the authentic probe sections showing the malformed row and repaired row; add a small byte-layout diagram labeled explanatory.
visual_before: Invalid row stride, point capacity, field layout, byte order or divisor is rejected.
visual_after: Correct padded rows pack four points; one NaN reduces the packed cloud to three.

title: Degenerate overlap and unstable filtering
symptom: Degenerate boxes, unstable overlap calculations or stale outputs could undermine filtering.
explanation: Rotated IoU needs robust geometry handling. Suppression should reject invalid configuration, preserve deterministic score ties and replace previous-frame output even for an empty frame.
steps: Validate finite centers, dimensions and yaw; require positive dimensions.
Compute rotated overlap using bounded polygon clipping.
Validate IoU threshold and top-N before suppression.
Use stable score ordering and clear the output on every attempt.
Check touching, contained, rotated, degenerate and random boxes.
verification: The current-source probe returned IoU=0 for zero-length geometry, rejected a negative NMS threshold and changed a one-box output to zero on an empty frame. Fresh geometry tests passed 15 cases including 2,000 randomized comparisons.
remaining_limit: Robust suppression does not move inaccurate boxes or establish detector accuracy.
visual_suggestion: Capture actual invalid-threshold and empty-output results; illustrate touching/overlapping footprints with a clearly labeled vector geometry diagram.
visual_before: Negative NMS threshold is rejected; zero-length geometry safely yields zero overlap.
visual_after: Valid suppression returns one box; a subsequent empty input clears it.

Keep the production policy explicit; evaluate a proposed change on tuning data before deployment.

title: Repeated allocation and stream ownership
symptom: Per-frame allocations, resource lifetime ambiguity and unchecked output counts could create stale data or unsafe copies.
explanation: Owned persistent resources remove repeated allocation. The runtime copies the result count first, checks it against capacity and only then copies box rows; serious GPU-work failure latches the runtime as faulted.
steps: Create and own the runtime, engine, context, stream and buffers once.
Reuse buffers and clear input padding/output count for each cloud.
Copy and validate the output count before copying rows.
Validate decoded classes, geometry and scores before publication.
Drain work during failure unwinding and require restart after a fault.
verification: The freshly compiled probe rejected counts -1 and 11 for capacity 10, then accepted count 10. Fresh output-contract tests passed; historical GPU smoke exercised repeated inference and cleanup.
remaining_limit: The current probe validates pure CPU count behavior, not injected GPU faults or complete resource/memory safety.
visual_suggestion: Capture authentic rejected/accepted count output and illustrate count-first transfer; use saved smoke output for repeated GPU execution claims.
visual_before: Counts below zero or above engine capacity are rejected before box-row transfer.
visual_after: A count equal to capacity is accepted; GPU fault handling remains a separate limit.

title: Real SDK version-macro and profiler incompatibilities
symptom: Actual TensorRT headers used macro aliases, and TensorRT 10.16 rejected setting the context profiler to null.
explanation: Parsing a literal version from a header was insufficient. The build now asks the preprocessor; the runtime keeps an owned profiler attached and gates its accumulation.
steps: Evaluate NV_TENSORRT_MAJOR with a compiler preprocessor guard.
Reject unsupported major versions before building the runtime.
Keep the profiler alive for the context lifetime.
Toggle accumulation instead of passing null.
Run actual SDK smoke checks; record callback overhead as unresolved.
verification: A compiler-only control using macro aliases rejected major 8 with TensorRT 10 required and accepted major 10. The historical record explains the null-profiler failure and subsequent GPU smoke success.
remaining_limit: The null-profiler GPU failure was not rerun. Callback overhead is not proven absent when timing accumulation is disabled.
visual_suggestion: Capture real compiler rejection and clean alias acceptance; describe profiler failure using dated source/log evidence, not a fabricated screenshot.
visual_before: Synthetic major-8 header is rejected by the same preprocessor guard used in CMake.
visual_after: Macro-aliased major 10 passes; historical null-profiler fix retains an owned profiler.
